chunks: Tamim ibn Abd Allah ibn Tamim al-Qurashi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me from Hamdan ibn Sulayman al-Naysaburi, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Jahm, who said: I attended the gathering of al-Ma'mun, and Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon them) was with him.

Al-Ma'mun said to him: 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, is it not from your saying that the Prophets are infallible?' He replied: 'Yes.' He asked him about some verses of the Quran, and among what he asked was: 'Tell me about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High, regarding Ibrahim: So when the night overshadowed him, he saw a star; said he: Is this my Lord?'

Al-Rida (peace be upon him) responded: 'Ibrahim (peace be upon him) came across three types of people: one type worshipped Venus, one worshipped the moon, and one worshipped the sun. This was when he came out of the den in which he was hidden. So when the night overshadowed him and he saw Venus, he said: This is my Lord, as a denial and inquiry. So when the star set, he said: I do not love the setting one, because setting is an attribute of the created (muhdath) and not from the attributes of the Eternal (qadim).'

So when he saw the moon rising, he said: This is my Lord, as a denial and inquiry. So when it set, he said: If my Lord had not guided me, I should certainly be of the erring people. So when morning came, he saw the sun rising and said: This is my Lord. This is greater than Venus and the moon. He said this as a denial and inquiry, not as information and affirmation.

So when it set, he said to the three types of people from the worshippers of Venus, the moon, and the sun: O my people! Surely I am clear of what you set up (with Allah). Surely I have turned myself, being upright, wholly to Him who originated the Heavens and the Earth, and I am not of the polytheists.

Ibrahim (peace be upon him) intended by what he said to clarify for them the invalidity of their religion, and to prove to them that worship is not due to that which has the attribute of Venus, the moon, and the sun. Rather, worship is due only to its Creator and the Creator of the Heavens and the Earth. The argument he brought forth against his people was what Allah, the Mighty and High, inspired and granted him, as Allah said: And this was Our argument which we gave to Ibrahim against his people.

Al-Ma'mun said: 'For Allah's sake, continue, O son of the Messenger of Allah!' The hadith is long; we have extracted from it the required passage. I have transmitted it in its entirety in the book 'Uyun Akhbar al-Rida (peace be upon him).'
ai.seo_question: How did Prophet Ibrahim use the setting of celestial bodies to prove they are not God?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this dialogue in *al-Tawhid* to illustrate the principle of *al-Ankar wa al-Istikhbar* (denial and inquiry), clarifying that Ibrahim’s repeated 'This is my Lord' was a rhetorical strategy to engage his polytheist contemporaries before refuting them. This exegesis underscores the Shia theological distinction between the created nature of celestial bodies (*muhdath*) and the eternal attribute of the Creator (*qadim*), serving as a logical proof for monotheism.
